title: Adjustment Disorder - Treatment and Management
content:
DOCUMENT TYPE: Treatment

FIRST-LINE TREATMENT: Brief psychotherapy focused on the stressor. Cognitive-behavioral or problem-solving approaches. Supportive therapy to process the change and build coping. Short-term (6-12 sessions) often sufficient.

SECOND-LINE / ESCALATION: If symptoms persist or meet criteria for another disorder (MDD, GAD), treat the comorbid condition with standard first-line therapies (SSRI + longer CBT). Pharmacotherapy rarely first-line unless severe insomnia or anxiety interfering with function.

RED FLAGS: Symptoms lasting >6 months after stressor resolution, emergence of suicidal ideation, marked functional decline, or new psychotic features. Reassess for missed MDD or PTSD.

PATIENT-LANGUAGE EXAMPLES: "I just need help getting through this transition", "The stress is too much right now".

PROVENANCE: APA Clinical Practice Guideline for treatment of adults with PTSD and related disorders (adjusted for adjustment). Systematic reviews support time-limited, stressor-focused interventions over long-term medication.
